title: Pipelines without secrets
scenario: "Pen-test finding: any branch can run a job with environment: lab and receive a token with Contributor on the subscription. Close it without adding secrets." — Red team report
mission: Restrict which branches can deploy to the lab environment and prove the OIDC trust is exactly the three expected subjects.
objectives: Read federated credential subjects and map them to GitHub job contexts
Discuss splitting plan and apply identities

prerequisites.notes: gh CLI signed in with admin rights on the repository.

steps.title: Opening incident: the plan jobs cannot log in
steps.detail: Every terraform plan job on pull requests fails with AADSTS700213 (no matching federated identity record). Diagnose it first with Observation → Hypothesis → Test → Evidence: read the failing log, list the trusted subjects, read the repository OIDC subject customization (gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/oidc/customization/sub), then fix the subjects in 05-identity (a tenant change: apply only with an explicit OK).

steps.title: List the trust
steps.detail: List the federated credentials of app-mfs-github-actions and map each subject to the job that can present it.
steps.command: az ad app federated-credential list --id <github_client_id> -o table

steps.title: Confirm there are no secrets
steps.detail: Check that the app has no password credentials.

steps.title: Restrict the environment
steps.detail: Configure the lab environment so only protected branches (main) can deploy to it. Use gh api — no portal clicks.

steps.title: Design the split
steps.detail: Write 5 lines: how would a read-only "plan" identity and a privileged "apply" identity map to subjects and roles?

criteria.text: Exactly three federated subjects: pull_request, ref:refs/heads/main, environment:lab
The GitHub app has no client secret
The lab environment only allows deployments from protected branches
The lab environment still requires a reviewer

expectedResult: A job on a feature branch can no longer obtain the environment:lab token.

concepts.title: OIDC federation in one paragraph
concepts.body: Instead of storing a client secret, GitHub gives each job a short-lived signed token describing *who* is running (repository, branch, environment). Entra ID trusts that token if its `subject` matches a *federated credential* on the app, and returns an Azure token. No secret ever exists.

concepts.title: The subject is the security boundary
concepts.body: Typical subjects: `repo:<owner>/<repo>:pull_request`, `repo:<owner>/<repo>:ref:refs/heads/main`, `repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:lab`. A job that declares `environment: lab` presents the environment subject — so whoever can run a job with that environment gets those permissions. The environment itself must therefore restrict *which branches* can use it and *who approves*.

concepts.title: Environment protection rules
concepts.body: A GitHub environment can have required reviewers and a *deployment branch policy*: either "protected branches only" or a list of custom branch patterns. A job from any other branch cannot even start in that environment.

example.title: reading an environment's rules with the API
example.body: The GitHub API returns the protection of an environment. Look for `protection_rules` (reviewers) and `deployment_branch_policy` (null = any branch):

glossary.def: Trust entry on an Entra app: issuer + subject + audience accepted instead of a secret.
Claim in the OIDC token identifying the job context; must match exactly.
Environment rule: a human must approve before the job runs.

recovery: If a workflow on main stops deploying, check that main is protected — protected_branches policy only matches protected branches.
dont: Do not add a client secret
Do not remove the reviewer rule
Do not widen subjects with wildcards
hints: Which GitHub setting decides which branches may use an environment?
The environments API accepts deployment_branch_policy with protected_branches and custom_branch_policies.
gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/environments/lab with reviewers and deployment_branch_policy[protected_branches]=true.

interview.question: How does a GitHub workflow authenticate to Azure without secrets, and what stops another branch from impersonating your deploy job?
followUps: What is in the OIDC token subject?
Why separate plan and apply identities?

debrief: The subject is the trust boundary: Entra only exchanges a GitHub token whose sub matches exactly. environment:lab is presented by any job that declares environment: lab, so the environment itself must restrict branches and require reviewers. A stronger design uses a Reader-only identity for PR plans and a privileged identity only for environment:lab.

checker.plan: Read-only: az ad app federated-credential list, az ad app credential list, gh api repos/<repo>/environments/lab.
